connections.pathList: Connections from the C5 to the component
connections.startInternal: These connections are already on the Pulsar C5. Advance to see what each signal does.
connections.startExternal: Unplug USB before adding wires. Advance to see each connection in order.
connections.doneInternal: These paths are built into the board; there are no jumper wires to add.
connections.doneExternal: Check the physical wires against this diagram before reconnecting USB.

note.userLed: GPIO27 drives the soldered-on user LED. It also serves as the microSD clock when the card is in use.
note.boot: The BOOT button pulls GPIO28 low when pressed. Do not hold it during reset unless you want download mode.
note.rgb: GPIO0 carries the data for the on-board RGB LED (WS2812). On the header it is the D2/RGB pad.
note.potGround: Connect the remaining outer leg of the potentiometer to GND.
note.sda: GPIO2 carries data to the on-board I²C sensors. The QWIIC connector uses a different bus.
note.scl: GPIO3 supplies the sensor bus clock. The on-board pull-ups are already fitted.
note.sdClock: GPIO27 clocks the card and is shared with the user LED, so the LED can flicker during card access.
note.sdMosi: GPIO7 carries data from the ESP32-C5 to the card.
note.sdMiso: GPIO26 carries data from the card back to the ESP32-C5.
note.sdSelect: GPIO23 selects the microSD card for each SPI transfer.
note.uart: With USB unplugged, place one jumper between the two pins shown. For MicroPython, use A2/GPIO4 and A3/GPIO5; never bridge TX0 and RX0.

materials.intro: UNIT Electronics products suggested for this lab. Check the connector and product variant before ordering; current prices and availability are on the product page.

potentiometer.name: 3-pin WH148 potentiometer
potentiometer.why: The adjustable analog input for P3.

microsd.name: Kingston microSD card
microsd.why: Use the card in the Pulsar C5 slot for P5; choose a capacity and format it as FAT32.

ch340e.name: UNIT CH340E USB-to-TTL module
ch340e.why: For a later external UART experiment. P6 loopback itself only needs one jumper; check 3.3 V signal levels before connecting.

qwiicCable.name: QWIIC / STEMMA QT 4-pin cable
qwiicCable.why: Select the QWIIC-to-QWIIC or QWIIC-to-Dupont variant that fits your wiring. It does not plug directly onto bare PN532 or OLED pins.

oled.name: 128×64 I²C OLED, SSD1315
oled.why: UNIT lists this display as SSD1315 and documents Arduino SSD1306-library use. O1/D2 use SSD1306 code; check the 0x3C address and test the MicroPython variant.

qwiicExpander.name: UNIT I²C QWIIC expander
qwiicExpander.why: Adds QWIIC sockets and header connections when sharing the bus. Its header pins are supplied unsoldered.

st7735.name: 0.96-inch 80×160 ST7735 TFT
st7735.why: The SPI display used in O2 and O3; follow the Pulsar C5 wiring in those lessons.

bmi270.name: UNIT DevLab BMI270 IMU
bmi270.why: The motion sensor for D1. Use I²C and check the module’s I²C solder bridge before wiring QWIIC.

temt600.name: UNIT DevLab TEMT600 light sensor
temt600.why: The I²C module for D2: UNIT documents DDP 1.0, factory address 0x20, device ID 0x0102, and ADC read command 0x60. Use this DevLab version; an analog-only version cannot run the example.

pn532.name: PN532 NFC/RFID reader V3
pn532.why: The I²C reader for R1–R8. UNIT says the package includes one MIFARE card and one key fob.

rfidCard.name: 13.56 MHz MIFARE S50 card
rfidCard.why: An extra test card. In R5, write only to a disposable card whose old contents you do not need.

rfidFob.name: 13.56 MHz RFID/NFC key fob
rfidFob.why: An extra UID for inventory, door and card-friends exercises; the PN532 package already includes one.

inmp441.name: INMP441 I²S microphone
inmp441.why: The digital microphone supported by the current sound examples. S8 requires it, and S2 uses it for dB SPL.

sph0645.name: SPH0645 I²S microphone
sph0645.why: For a future adaptation: the current sound firmware is configured for INMP441 and does not support this microphone directly.

ics43434.name: UNIT DevLab ICS-43434 I²S microphone
ics43434.why: An S1 extension for Pulsar C5: open the web serial level example. It requires a C5 MicroPython build with machine.I2S enabled; the bundled generic image does not enable it. The six-pin I²S connector is not QWIIC.

max98357.name: MAX98357 I²S audio amplifier
max98357.why: The amplifier used by the current playback examples; pair it with a suitable speaker.

speaker.name: 4 Ω / 3 W speaker
speaker.why: Select the 4 Ω, 3 W variant for the MAX98357 amplifier in S7 and S8.

es8311.name: UNIT DevLab ES8311 codec guide
es8311.why: Documentation for a different audio codec. S7/S8 use MAX98357; ES8311 requires different wiring and firmware.
